decisions.reason: As a floor-level shower drainage system, it remains closely tied to the firm's declared move toward low-profile, accessible bathroom solutions, so prior development effort and strategic fit still favor retention despite some uncertainty.
Because management publicly framed this designer shower drainage line as a flagship for the firm's direction, the need to justify that commitment makes withdrawal within a year unlikely.

This shower element with integrated slope supports installation ease and renovation use cases central to the firm's positioning, so sunk development costs and continued strategic relevance argue for keeping it.

Although a backflow-protected basement floor drain is somewhat less central to the bathroom-focused future direction, its prominent launch, technical specialization, and invested resources still make management more likely to continue than to withdraw it.
